source.title: Stability and Generalization of Graph Convolutional Neural Networks

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; some PDF extraction artifacts and garbled symbols occur, but the relevant experimental descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper empirically compares generalization gaps across graph convolution filters and datasets, and measures parameter stability after changing one training example. This is a different model family and setting from the claim’s listed versions, but the measured training–test gap bears on V7’s generalization-gap subject only indirectly; none of the versions names graph filters or graph neural networks. Its empirical results do not test the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: Reports graph-filter comparisons for generalization gap and weight-parameter stability on Citeseer, Cora, and Pubmed. The paper’s theoretical statements and cited results are not empirical rows. Figure 1 describes the relative gaps but supplies no exact values in the text; Figure 2 describes relative parameter divergence but does not measure the magnitude-aware perturbation measure in V7.
record.test_reason: The study measures graph-filter normalization effects on loss gaps and sensitivity to changing one training sample. These results test none of V1–V8. In particular, training-data sensitivity is distinct from V7's magnitude-scaled weight perturbations; measuring a generalization gap alone does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive stability and generalization bounds for single-layer GCNNs under their smoothness, Lipschitz and feature-normalization assumptions, with bounds depending on the graph filter's largest absolute eigenvalue or singular value. They argue that appropriately normalized filters provide graph-size-independent bounds, and report empirical gap and parameter-divergence comparisons consistent with this analysis.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes and evaluates single-layer graph convolutional networks in semi-supervised node learning, comparing graph filters; the claim versions concern other architectures, optimizers, regularizers, measures, or memorization effects.
record.method_sensitivity: Graph filter normalization and dataset (Citeseer, Cora, Pubmed) change the reported gap and parameter-stability behavior.

fits_no_version.finding: Unnormalized graph filters produce larger absolute training–test cross-entropy gaps than normalized filters on Citeseer, Cora and Pubmed.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the tested single-layer GCNN recipe on citation networks, graph-filter normalization is associated with smaller training–test loss gaps.

fits_no_version.finding: After one training sample is changed, unnormalized-filter models exhibit large parameter divergence, while normalized-filter parameter differences quickly approach a fixed value.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Graph-filter normalization affects learned-parameter sensitivity to a one-sample training-set change in the tested single-layer GCNNs.

record.peer_reviewed: KDD ’19: The 25th ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining
record.problems: The empirical results are shown in figures without exact numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The experiments use only three citation-network datasets and a single-layer GCNN setup. Parameter stability is evaluated via L2-norm difference, which is distinct from the magnitude-aware sharpness measure in V7.
record.rows_left_out: No reported empirical comparisons meeting the row criteria were left out. Theoretical bounds and cited prior work are not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label held-out generalization.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed to fit training data.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or optimizer modifications.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout effects across training-set sizes and interactions with augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation tolerance, its association with generalization gaps at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The exclusion rests on the measured constructs and comparisons, not merely on using graph networks. Neither the generalization-gap results nor the one-sample sensitivity experiment measures V7's sharpness construct. The discussion and citations of original generalization studies supply no additional tests of their claims.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under tuning choices.
Large versus small batch size and recipe adaptation.
Dropout effects and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness perturbation measure and its ranking against norm- or margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
